label: EU(7)-PIM: verapamil and diltiazem
title: Verapamil and diltiazem
statement: The 2015 list flags oral verapamil and diltiazem for review in older people because they can slow the pulse and worsen constipation. It suggests alternative blood pressure medicines for verapamil used for hypertension. When either drug is used for atrial fibrillation, review the rate-control plan, pulse, symptoms and ventricular function before considering a change.

plain_summary: Verapamil and diltiazem can worsen constipation and slow the heart too much in older people.

medicine_groups.name: Verapamil and diltiazem
medicine_groups.note: All oral forms count, immediate-release and sustained-release. Amlodipine, felodipine and nifedipine are not in this group. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too. Count an oral combination that contains verapamil or diltiazem.

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when the person is aged 65 or older and at least one Group A medicine (verapamil or diltiazem, by mouth) is supplied. If age is missing and the supply otherwise qualifies, report only a possible finding and ask the pharmacist to confirm whether the person is 65 or older. A recorded age below 65 gives no finding.
cannot_be_seen: Why it was prescribed (for example angina, a heart rhythm problem or blood pressure), the person's heart rate, and whether they have constipation.
ask_the_gp: Could we review the indication, pulse, constipation and symptoms? If the medicine is used for atrial fibrillation, could we review the rate-control plan and ventricular function before considering a change?
